rationale: The chosen topology leverages a folded common-source architecture with a resistive-capacitive feedback network to achieve wideband input matching (S11 ≤ -15 dB across 0.5–3 GHz), low noise figure (NF ≤ 2.5 dB), and high gain (S21 ≥ 16 dB) while operating under a 5 mA current budget. The folded structure enables a balanced differential-like operation with single-ended inputs and outputs, reducing noise and improving linearity. The feedback network (Rf, Cf) from drain to gate provides frequency-dependent gain control and stabilizes the input match across the band, fulfilling the tight S11 requirement without inductors. The topology avoids floating nodes, respects the device budget (≤16 transistors), and is fully inductorless—meeting the hard corner constraint. This design prioritizes input match and noise performance by ensuring the input is driven through a low-impedance path while maintaining a high transconductance-to-current ratio. The feedback is tuned via Rf and Cf to flatten S21 ripple and achieve gain stability, avoiding the pitfalls of overdriving the input stage or starving the swing stage.
